title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 206 (Power to call for information, inspect books and conduct inquiries)

content.overview: Section 206 empowers the Registrar, on the basis of information available or received, or on scrutiny of any document, to call for information or explanation, or to inspect books and papers of a company. Where the Registrar is satisfied on the basis of information so available or furnished that further information or explanation is required, he may by written order call for such further information or explanation. He may also require production of books and papers. Where he considers further inquiry necessary, he may inquire into the affairs of the company. The company and its officers must furnish the information and produce the books. The Registrar may obtain information from past employees and agents as the section allows. This is the inquiry and inspection step; formal investigation is under sections 210 and 212.
content.glance: Registrar may call for information/explanation, inspect books and papers, and inquire into affairs; company and officers must comply; may seek info from past employees/agents; distinct from formal investigation under ss. 210/212.
content.study: Where on a scrutiny of any document filed by a company or on any information received by him, the Registrar is of the opinion that any further information or explanation or any further documents relating to the company is necessary, he may by a written order call for the same. On receipt of such information or explanation, the Registrar may require the production of books and papers. If the Registrar is satisfied that the information or explanation is not satisfactory, or that the affairs of the company are being conducted in a fraudulent manner or in a manner prejudicial to public interest or to the interests of the company, he may report the matter to the Central Government for investigation. Separately, the Registrar may, on a written order, inspect books and papers and conduct an inquiry. Current-law framing: identify the Registrar’s written order; map the information, inspection or inquiry power invoked; confirm the company’s duty to furnish and produce; distinguish the step from formal investigation under ss. 210 and 212.

sections.heading: Call for Information
sections.body: Registrar may by written order call for further information, explanation or documents relating to the company on scrutiny or information received.

sections.heading: Inspection of Books
sections.body: Registrar may require production of books and papers and inspect them.

sections.heading: Inquiry
sections.body: Where further inquiry is considered necessary, the Registrar may inquire into the affairs of the company.

sections.heading: Duty to Comply
sections.body: Company and officers must furnish information and produce books; Registrar may obtain records from past employees and agents as allowed.

provisions.title: Power to call for information, inspect books and conduct inquiries

examples.title: Written order for explanation
examples.body: On scrutiny of an annual return, the Registrar issues a written order calling for further explanation of related-party disclosures. The company must furnish the explanation under s. 206.

examples.title: Not yet an investigation
examples.body: The Registrar inspects books under s. 206 and is dissatisfied. Reporting the matter to the Central Government for investigation engages ss. 210/212; the s. 206 step itself is inspection and inquiry, not formal investigation.

hypotheticals.question: May the company refuse a s. 206 information request because no formal investigation has been ordered?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 206 is an independent power to call for information, inspect books and inquire. Formal investigation under ss. 210/212 is a later, separate step. Refusal to comply with a lawful s. 206 order attracts the consequences the Act provides.

distinctions.title: Call for information and inquiry (s. 206) vs investigation (ss. 210/212)
distinctions.left: Registrar’s power to call for info, inspect books and inquire
distinctions.right: Formal investigation ordered by Central Government / SFIO route

misconceptions.trap: Section 206 only applies after a formal investigation is ordered.
misconceptions.correction: Section 206 is the front-end power to call for information, inspect and inquire. Formal investigation is under sections 210 and 212.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 206 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify Registrar’s written order. II. Map information/inspection/inquiry power. III. Confirm duty to comply. IV. Distinguish investigation. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Order facts; power invoked; compliance status; precise relief.
